title: Lecturer of the Magic Academy
text: “What is it now, Rival! If you’re picking a fight with me, I’ll gladly accept, I say!”
Even so, teaching happens to be one of my specialties, I say. After all, in this loop it was me who taught magic to Father and the others.
“Well, you could probably manage decently with men and beastmen, but everyone else? Nano, isn’t that a bit hopeless?”
“Agreed… Honestly, knowing him, he’d probably just brute-force everything. I can easily picture him blowing up a mountain and calling it a ‘demonstration.’”
“Hmm, well, that would be impressive in its own way, but if we’re leaving it to Motoyasu-kun, I think we’d need someone like Yuki-chan keeping an eye on him, or it’ll get rough…”
“It’s pretty much guaranteed he’ll cause some unnecessary uproar… which, I suppose, is exactly why the arrow of fate points at me…”
Itsuki is muttering under his breath about how the reasoning checks out, but how rude! This Motoyasu fully intends to accomplish anything Father commands of him, I say!
“Father, should I be the one to go, I wonder?”
“No, if Motoyasu-kun goes, Yuki-chan’s going to collapse from overwork trying to manage you. Besides, her race is coming up soon.”

Incidentally, Yuki-chan is currently over in Zeltoble, training alongside the Filolial breeders and the Sage to prepare for her upcoming race, I say. She trains her body every single day with the fierce determination of a boxer devoted to the ring. According to Yuki-chan herself, she wants to break the course record. Apparently her stoic dedication has been earning her quite a lot of new fans lately. And since she can also sing and dance, her popularity just keeps climbing, I say. Fleon-chan is also becoming the talk of the town in various places—little by little, the whole world’s admiration for Filolial-sama is growing.
“By the way, how do things stand in the other worlds, Gaelion-san?”
“In the very first world, the wild Naofumi one, nano, it was Naofumi who got nominated. Nano, guess that’s just the difference in how much each of us accomplished.”
Father in that very first world was evaluated head and shoulders above the rest of us Heroes, after all, I say.

“Well, in that first world there was also the Wise Sage-King, so wild Naofumi was in a position where he could just say ‘too much trouble’ and get away with it—so a lot of the time, other Heroes went in his place, nano.”

“How to put this… they’re supposedly the same person, but he sounds far lazier than the Naofumi-san we know. No, wait—in this case, I suppose ‘busy with other things’ is the more accurate way to phrase it?”
“That’s exactly right, nano.”

There’s no doubt Father was busy with all sorts of things back then. I, meanwhile, was ordered to look after Filolial-sama and did my absolute best at it, I say! Those were truly delightful times, I say.
“In other worlds too, it was often a similar story—Heroes getting called in as lecturers, nano.”
“In Filoko’s era too, there was a prestigious school-kyu.”
Here Filoko-chan kindly filled us in about the academy as well. I see—so it’s an institution with quite the long tradition.

“Is that so. Well, since we’ve been asked, maybe we should just go along with it? Itsuki and Ren are technically still high schoolers age-wise, so instead of thinking of it as ‘being a lecturer,’ why not just go in with the mindset of being a student?”

“With everything that’s happened, I’d completely forgotten I was ever a student in the first place. Same goes for Ren-san, I imagine… Though, weren’t you and the others university students too, Naofumi-san?”

“I went to a pretty third-rate university and mostly just coasted through—though the professors and lecturers and classmates were always dragging me into things or asking favors. I think I got treated pretty well, actually.”
“Specifically, how so?”
Ah, Father’s student life. It’s something gentle Father would occasionally tell us about once peace had settled in, if you asked him, I say.
“I heard in another world that he got some slack cut on his course credits and things like that, I say.”
“Ah, said that too, nano. Gaelion remembers hearing that as well, nano.”
“Ah, so Motoyasu-kun and Gaelion-chan already know, huh. Yeah. In exchange for doing various favors for people. I like to think I handled that side of things pretty well.”
“As mentioned before, was it mostly things like being brought unusual ingredients and asked to cook with them?”
Itsuki’s instincts are sharp as ever, I say.

“Yeah. Ostrich meat and all sorts of things. The most common request was something small, like turning salmon roe sacs into soy-sauce-marinated ikura. One lecturer even asked me if I could recreate his late wife’s cooking.”

Apparently Father had some connection to an elderly lecturer at his university who asked him for that favor. After hearing all sorts of stories about her cooking, he supposedly pieced together the recipe, recreated it, and the man was absolutely delighted, I say.
“Now that I think about it… where exactly did you fall short of being a ‘normie,’ Naofumi-san?”
“Well, I didn’t have a girlfriend or anything? And I kept a fair bit of distance from the genuinely popular crowd.”
“Naofumi-san. If you compare yourself to Motoyasu-san and call yourself not a normie, that might technically be true, but you’re setting the bar awfully high.”
“Whether the Motoyasu-kun we know counts as a ‘normie’… I guess that’d have to be past tense now…”

“Normie” is a term Ren and Itsuki use too, referring to someone back in Japan who lived a fulfilling life. Me, a normie? I never once thought of myself that way in the slightest, I say—though I suppose I did throw myself into all sorts of entanglements with pigs as my top priority. These days it’s nothing but a string of thoroughly nauseating, tiresome days with those pigs. If I’m going to spend precious memory capacity on such things, I ought to be filling it instead with memories of Filo-tan and Father and everyone else, I say.
“How to put it… Naofumi-san, if you hadn’t come to another world, I feel like you’d have gotten a girlfriend eventually, given some time.”
“Ohh? Naofumi-chaaan?”

Here Older Sister comes sidling up to Father, I say. The newborn baby is fast asleep, breathing peacefully. Incidentally, before this little one and Panda’s child drifted off, about three Filolial-sama wore themselves out playing with them. Such outrageous stamina, I say.
“Naofumi-chan really is charming, isn’t he—even Big Sister finds him quite lovely.”
“I—I don’t know about that. In that other world, I think I was more like… a decent errand boy at best? There were a lot of people like that around.”

“Perhaps the women there had a favorable impression of you, but only saw you as ‘keep-around’ material. If word had simply gotten out that you had a girlfriend or something, there’s a good chance a wave of sudden popularity would’ve hit you…”

“Itsuki? Why are you looking at me so suspiciously? Honestly, setting Motoyasu-kun aside, with a face as good as yours, Itsuki, you could get girlfriends far more easily than I ever could. Same goes for you, Ren.”
Here, for some reason, both Ren and Itsuki fall silent, I say.
“In Ren’s case it’s probably mostly the childhood-friend thing, but what about you, Itsuki?”
“…I was a low-ability holder, remember. I never got any recognition among the people around me. Though, admittedly, that’s not the only reason.”
“Oh, that reminds me, Bow Hero.”
Rival asks, tapping its head repeatedly as if trying to jog its memory, I say.
“…What is it?”
“Nano, I recall hearing—Gaelion remembers hearing, nano—that you had a relative by blood connection who was a high-ability holder.”
The instant that was murmured, Itsuki’s eyebrows twitched upward ever so slightly.
“I don’t know which loop’s version of me let that slip, but… what a bothersome topic to bring up.”
“What what? Some kind of heavy backstory?”

“No… it’s nothing that serious. I just had a relative, younger than me, who possessed a powerful unique ability. It’s not that child’s fault at all, but because of it, I frequently got dragged into troublesome situations.”
“I-Itsuki-sama’s original world? I’d love to hear about it!”
Riska raises her hand, pestering Itsuki to tell her more, I say.
“I’d rather not, if possible. Rishia-san, all I meant was that I’m someone who, much like you, grew up always looking upward at someone ahead of them.”
Itsuki, quite unusually, seems desperate to smoothly change the subject, I say.
“Ahh… the whole ‘compared to your talented relative’ thing… I get how that feels, since my little brother was talented too.”
“I wonder if Big Sister would’ve put Raphtalia-chan through the same kind of hardship, if she’d had a younger sibling… No, there’s absolutely no way Big Sister could ever do that to Raphtalia-chan.”
“Raph.”
Older Sister murmurs this, gazing at Big Sister and the Raph-species. I’m sure Big Sister in this loop will turn out just fine, I say.
“It’s fine, isn’t it. Anyway, I’ll go ahead and be the one who goes to be the lecturer this time.”
It seems Itsuki would rather redirect his attention to something else than keep talking about his relatives back in Japan.

“Since it sounds like Itsuki’s okay with continuing, we could go with the Rafuemon material, or stick with the magic academy angle, but honestly, wouldn’t ‘Seven Mysteries of the Magic School’ feel more fitting?”
“Who told you to pick up that kind of joke?! If you actually go filming something like that, I will be furious!”
“So to begin with, what kind of school is this place?”
Father asks Éclair, I say.

“It’s a school located in a remote borderland far from Faubrey’s royal capital, more like a small town in its own right. Historically, it’s enrolled not just nobility from various countries, but many practitioners of magic besides.”
Éclair unrolls a map and points to the location, I say. I already had the place memorized, so I understood immediately, I say.
“Ah… I know where that is now. From the game, I mean.”
“Right. That spot. I sort of recognize it too.”
Specifically, the location overlaps perfectly with a town called the Magic Academy that I know from Emerald Online, I say.
“There’s a dungeon underground, isn’t there?”
“It’s a hunting ground crawling with undead and spirit-attribute monsters.”
“A hunting ground where you can secure monsters useful for Spirit Enchanting, I say.”
Back in the game days, the soul items you could obtain from monsters there were extremely valuable, so everyone flocked there hoping to strike it rich, I say.

“It’s a place where the earth’s mana flows powerfully. Because of the land’s unique properties, magic becomes remarkably easy to use there. It was once a battlefield in the past, and though it’s regularly purified, monsters still occasionally emerge from the caverns underground.”
“Sounds like a kind of fun place, actually. Like… I feel like I could even fight there myself, using healing magic against the undead.”
“Naofumi, unfortunately…”

Rival delivers a cruel pronouncement to Father, I say. Even I can’t bring myself to say this to Father, so I can’t exactly hold it against Rival for its line either, I say. Father’s healing aptitude is so thoroughly one-sided that, outside of ingredients and materials, he can’t induce activation, aging, or decomposition. In other words, he cannot deal damage to undead with healing magic, I say.
“Ah… I see.”
Father looks tremendously disappointed. Ngh… this is simply something Father cannot do, I say.
“So it’s that magic school, is it. There were quite a lot of quests there too, so I remember it well enough…”
“The question is whether it’s wise to act on game knowledge or not.”
“They just want someone to come as a lecturer to the academy there, so I don’t think we need to worry about the hunting ground or anything.”
“That’s true.”
“By the way, apparently Takt and Princess Malty were also once enrolled there.”
Apparently there’s an intention to publicize that everyone connected to Takt has been thoroughly cleared out, and that the place is now sound and healthy.
“Yeah… but just hearing who used to attend already gives me a bad feeling…”
“Waaah… I was enrolled there too…”
Itsuki turns to look at Riska after her remark.
“Eh? You too, Rishia-san?”
“I went home for a break during my year’s promotion, and then the whole ‘wave’ business happened, and I ended up on academic leave.”
“In that case, I suppose you’ll be resuming your studies there, Rishia-san?”
“Y-yes. I was always good at the written exams, so I’ve fulfilled my graduation credits, but…”
Notably, she doesn’t mention practicals—very Riska of her.
“Couldn’t Rishia just present a thesis on quadruple-mixed-attribute magic as her practical, nano? Nano, she’s bound to score more than well enough.”
“I-it’s not that impressive, really…”

“Still… if we bring Rishia-san to the academy while she’s being all friendly with Itsuki, wouldn’t that get complicated? Like… either she gets treated with reverence for being a Hero’s companion, or she gets targeted with jealousy, right?”
“Waaaahh…”
“Nano, I don’t see the harm in bringing Rishia along. Nano, she’d probably be low-maintenance and genuinely helpful.”
Rival appears to be advocating for Riska and Itsuki going to the academy together, I say.
“…True. Still… I think it might be better this time if Rishia-san stays behind and watches the house with Rafuemon-san.”

But it seems Itsuki wants to leave Riska behind to mind the house. Riska is quite capable, after all—the reasoning being that she’d likely do more good handling things around the village than attending the academy. Lately the Doctor has also been coming by the village from time to time, so learning directly from her ought to cover her studies quite sufficiently, I say.
“B-but I can’t stand the thought of Itsuki-sama having a hard time without me watching over him…”
“That feeling alone is more than enough. Anyway, I understand about the lecturer request that came to Éclair-san and the others. I’ll go as a trial run. We can decide what to do from there.”
And so it was decided that Itsuki would go to the academy, I say.
“So, everyone—starting with Naofumi-san—please stop turning me and Rafuemon-san into material for weird jokes. That’s all I have to say.”
“We are grateful for Kawasumi-dono’s cooperation.”
Éclair offers thanks on everyone’s behalf, I say.
“Nano nano. Nano, glad to hear things got settled so nicely-nano~.”
“The Bow Hero’s teaching career begins-kyu.”
And so, with Rival and Filoko-chan tossing in remarks that felt oddly pointed, the matter of who would go serve as lecturer at the magic school was finally decided, I say.
